subject: Food Science
title: Mad Cow Disease Crisis
description: A quick win: understand Mad Cow Disease Crisis.

hook.text: In 1996, the British government admitted BSE (mad cow disease) had jumped to humans.

buildup.text: BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy) is caused by prions—misfolded proteins that destroy brain tissue.

discovery.text: BSE spread because cattle were fed meat-and-bone meal from infected animals—a practice that turned herbivores into involuntary.

twist.text: The UK government denied BSE risk to humans for 10 years (1986–1996) to protect the beef industry.

climax.text: 4.4 million UK cattle were slaughtered. Meat-and-bone meal feeding was banned globally.

punchline.text: Feeding cows to cows created a disease that cooking can't kill.

quiz.question: Why couldn't BSE be eliminated by normal food safety methods?
options: Prions are misfolded proteins that can't be destroyed by cooking, freezing, or radiation
